thesis: The shared book is 100% cash (zero positions on $1000 sizing equity), so the aggressive-tier question this hour is whether to put risk on at all and in what form, not which name to rotate into. Only two items in the pack are decision-relevant and they cut both ways: the U.S. and China agreed to $60bn of tariff cuts on consumer goods with rare earths still unresolved and no movement on AI, Iran, or Taiwan (real de-escalation, modest in scope), against a 2026-09-27 column arguing the index rally is masking elevated oil, rising Treasury yields, and a Fed braced for further hikes. That is a two-sided macro tape and it argues for broad exposure at partial size rather than conviction in any single name. Everything else is retail personal-finance columns, ABS and trust 8-Ks with no equity read-through, routine Item 5.02 officer changes, and House PTRs from a week or more ago with no disclosed positions. I am specifically declining the three tempting single-name reads: Micron into its report is a binary event I would be gambling on, MongoDB down roughly 20% on its CEO leaving for Meta is a knife-catch where the move already happened and I have no price to size against, and the Nvidia valuation piece is an opinion column rather than a catalyst. So I propose beta: QQQ $300 (30% of sizing equity) for the tech and AI exposure the tape has kept paying, and VTI $250 (25%) as broad ballast that also picks up any tariff-cut relief in domestic consumer names. That leaves 55% deployed, 45% cash, 2 positions, well inside the shared execution caps of a 15% cash floor, 35% max single name, and 6 positions, so this proposal cannot by itself cause a whole-batch reject, and it preserves dry powder to concentrate if a genuine catalyst lands. With an hour to the close I am treating this as an opening allocation rather than a day trade, and I assume no fill until consensus and the book validator decide.
